The test image shows a soybean stem with prominent **white cottony mycelium** and large **black sclerotia** (hard, irregular black bodies) on the stem tissue, with surrounding brown/dead stem material and some still-green leaves.

The White Mold reference images are a strong match — identical white fluffy fungal growth and blue-black sclerotia on stems. The symptom description also aligns: "seeds may be replaced by sclerotia" and white cottony growth are hallmarks of Sclerotinia stem rot (White Mold).

Anthracnose shows dry brown/orange pods with small black spines — distinctly different.
